reader.requirement: At --std 85 PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1 (the single-name IS form, PROGRAM and COLLATING optional words) must make the alphabet's sequence (STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2, NATIVE, implementor-name or the literal phrase with THROUGH/ALSO) the program collating sequence; a name that is not an alphabet, and the 2002 alphabet-name-2/FOR forms, must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: ProgramCollatingNational2002: alphabet-name-2 and the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL forms refused below 2002
ComputerNameOptional2002: the clause without computer-name refused below 2002

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition/DialectLevel in SpecialNamesBinder.ResolveProgramCollating, ObjectComputerEmit, EmitCore.CollateArgFor: none; the resolution and the __COLLATE carrier are edition-independent
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 only the single-name IS form is accepted; the resolution of that form is identical at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f06_01 covers one literal alphabet with ALSO; THROUGH (descending), numeric ordinals, STANDARD-1 and the refusals are not exercised

reader.notes: ResolveProgramCollating sets Cfg.Collating to the alphabet's definition (null for an identity alphabet), ObjectComputerEmit emits it as __COLLATE and every alphanumeric comparison takes it through CollateArgFor. pcs5d prints a second, 2023-worded class-mismatch error beside the edition gate at 85; cosmetic, outside this rule.

refuter.evidence: r5a-001: ALPHABET REV IS "ZYX" 67 "A" (multi-character literal without THRU/ALSO, numeric ordinal 67 = B) as PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE: Z<Y<X<B<A<space all YES, and LOW-VALUE becomes 'Z' (LOW=Z YES, Z=LOWV YES). r5b-001: ALPHABET EB IS EBCDIC (implementor-name-2): '1'>'A' YES, 'a'<'Z' YES (EBCDIC order). r5c-001: ALPHABET IS STANDARD-2 with a NATIVE alphabet beside it: '1'<'A', 'a'>'Z' (ISO 646 order). Edition sites: SpecialNamesBinder.Alphabets gates (RangeInAlphabet2002, alphabet LOCALE <2002) are 2002-form refusals off the 1985 single-name path. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.4.4.4 GR5  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5
